target.title: fix: separate allowPluginSyntheticAuth from allowAuthProfileFallback in model auth
target.body:
## Summary

修复了 gateway 路由的模型调用无法解析插件合成认证（如 Anthropic Vertex 的 ADC）的问题。

## Root Cause

在 `src/agents/model-auth.ts:1646`，当 `allowAuthProfileFallback: false` 时（gateway 准备的路径调用），`allowPluginSyntheticAuth` 也被错误地设置为 `false`：

```typescript
allowPluginSyntheticAuth: params.allowAuthProfileFallback !== false,
```

这导致 `resolveSyntheticLocalProviderAuth` 跳过插件合成认证解析，因此插件的 `resolveSyntheticAuth` hook 根本没有机会执行。

## Fix

- 添加独立的 `allowPluginSyntheticAuth` 参数到 `resolveApiKeyForProvider` 和 `getApiKeyForModel` 函数
- 默认值为 `true`（通过 `?? true`），而不是从 `allowAuthProfileFallback` 派生
- 分离了两个概念：
  1. `allowAuthProfileFallback` - 是否允许从 auth-profiles.json 读取存储的用户配置 profile
  2. `allowPluginSyntheticAuth` - 是否允许调用插件的 `resolveSyntheticAuth` hook

## Testing

添加了回归测试证明：
- 当 `allowAuthProfileFallback: false` 但 `allowPluginSyntheticAuth` 未指定（默认 true）时，插件合成认证成功解析
- 当 `allowPluginSyntheticAuth: false` 明确设置时，插件合成认证被阻止

## Related Issues

Fixes: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/110103

target.title: fix(sessions): read pinned session-extension registry in upstream monitor
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`currentProviders()` in the session upstream-activity monitor read the **mutable** `getPluginRegistryState()?.activeRegistry` to discover session-catalog providers. A standalone plugin load/reload swaps `activeRegistry` (via `setActivePluginRegistry` → `syncTrackedSurface(state.sessionExtension, …)`), so the long-lived background monitor could observe a post-swap registry with no catalogs and silently stop watching upstream activity.

This is the same drift class fixed upstream in `session-catalog.ts`, which now reads the bootstrap-pinned `getActivePluginSessionExtensionRegistry()`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Read the pinned session-extension registry (`getActivePluginSessionExtensionRegistry()?.sessionCatalogs`) instead of the mutable `activeRegistry`. The monitor is a persistent loop with no request-scoped pin, so it must use the stable surface the gateway already pins at startup.

## User Impact

The upstream-activity monitor keeps watching the correct session catalogs across plugin-registry churn instead of observing an empty set. No config or protocol change; no migration.

## Evidence

- Regression test `session-upstream-monitor-pinned-registry.test.ts` "reads the pinned session-extension registry after active registry churn": pins a registry carrying the provider, swaps the mutable `activeRegistry` to an empty one, asserts the monitor still calls the pinned provider. **Red before the fix** (`checkUpstreamActivity` called 0 times), green after.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/sessions/session-upstream-monitor-pinned-registry.test.ts src/sessions/session-upstream-monitor.test.ts` → 1 + 17 passed.
- Verified `upstream/main` still reads the mutable `activeRegistry` (not yet fixed), so this PR is not a duplicate.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: The upstream monitor (`src/sessions/session-upstream-monitor.ts`) read the session-extension catalog from the wrong registry state accessor (`getPluginRegistryState().activeRegistry`), which did not reflect the pinned/active session-extension registry. It now reads via `getActivePluginSessionExtensionRegistry()` so `currentProviders()` returns the live session catalogs used for upstream activity probing.

Real environment tested: macOS 15, Node v24.18.0 (Homebrew node@24), vitest 4.1.9. The fix is exercised by the existing test suite which drives the real session state database (`openOpenClawStateDatabase`) against throwaway temp dirs and asserts monitor tick behavior end to end.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
- `npx vitest run src/sessions/session-upstream-monitor.test.ts`

Evidence after fix:
```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  17 passed (17)
```

Observed result after fix: All 17 integration tests pass, covering upsert/read/watch of session upstream links, missing-counter accounting, and the monitor tick that consumes the active session-extension catalog providers. The change swaps the registry accessor to the pinned/active one without altering the provider-mapping logic, so the tick now sees the correct live catalogs.

What was not tested: Live multi-plugin gateway deployment against a real plugin registry was not run (no plugin fixtures beyond the in-test catalog providers). The in-repo integration suite exercises the exact changed code path (the registry accessor call inside `currentProviders()`) against the real state database.

target.title: fix(ui): bound chat avatar metadata and image fetches
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`refreshChatAvatar` in `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-avatar.ts` issues two `fetch` calls — the avatar metadata lookup and the local avatar image download — **without any timeout or abort signal**. A stalled gateway leaves avatar resolution pending indefinitely, blocking the chat header update.

This is the same unbounded-network-operation class fixed across many `fix(...)` "bound X" PRs: a request with no `AbortSignal` can hang the caller forever.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add an `AbortController` + `setTimeout` watchdog (`CHAT_AVATAR_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000`) around both fetches, matching the Control UI convention used by `agent-select.ts` (`AGENT_SELECT_AVATAR_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS`). The timer is cleared in `finally`.

## User Impact

Avatar loading fails fast instead of hanging when the gateway is slow or unreachable.

## Evidence

- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-avatar.ts` on `main`: both `fetch` calls have no `signal`.
- Fix threads `controller.signal` into both requests and clears the timeout.

Co-Authored-By: opencode <noreply@opencode.ai>
## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: Chat avatar resolution (`refreshChatAvatar` in `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-avatar.ts`) hangs the chat header forever when the gateway/relay avatar-metadata endpoint never responds, because both the metadata fetch and the local image fetch have no abort signal.

Real environment tested: macOS 15, Node v24.18.0 (Homebrew node@24), vitest 4.1.9, local HTTP server (`node:http`) bound to 127.0.0.1:0. Real `fetch` is used against that server; only relative-URL resolution is bridged to the local origin. To keep Node's native `fetch` scheduling working, the normal-case test runs under real timers while the stalled-case test uses fake timers to fire the 30s watchdog without waiting in real time.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
- `npx vitest run ui/src/pages/chat/chat-avatar.test.ts`

Evidence after fix:
```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
 - aborts a stalled metadata fetch after the bound instead of hanging (pass)
 - still resolves a normal metadata + image round trip             (pass)
```

Observed result after fix: With the metadata endpoint accepting the connection but never ending the response, `refreshChatAvatar` returns via its abort/catch path after the 30s bound instead of remaining pending. With the endpoint returning 200 JSON plus a local image URL that also returns 200, `refreshChatAvatar` completes and sets the host avatar URL. Ordinary avatar loading is unaffected.

What was not tested: A full live Control UI browser session against a real gateway was not executed (no gateway credentials / headless browser in this environment). The proof exercises the exact production fetch/timeout/abort code path against a real local server, which is the behavior the change governs; the browser-only difference is relative-URL resolution, which is bridged in the test.

target.title: fix(voice-call): unref ngrok startup timeout, mark closed only on close event
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`startNgrokTunnel`'s 30s startup `setTimeout` was never `unref()`'d, so an abandoned tunnel promise kept the host process alive until the timer fired. On the timeout path the child was killed but `closed` was not set, leaving the `stop()` cleanup path inconsistent with the eventual `close` event.

## Why This Change Was Made

`unref()` the startup timer so it cannot pin the event loop, and mark the process `closed` on timeout so `stop()` does not try to re-kill an already-terminating child.

## User Impact

The voice-call tunnel startup no longer holds the process open when its caller has moved on; no change to successful tunnel startup.

## Evidence

- Regression test "unrefs the ngrok startup timeout so it cannot keep the host process alive": spies on `setTimeout` and asserts the returned timer's `unref()` is called. **Red before the fix** (`unref` called 0 times), green after.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/voice-call/src/tunnel.test.ts` → 16 passed.
- Verified `upstream/main` is byte-identical for this region (not yet fixed), so this PR is not a duplicate.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: `startNgrokTunnel` in `extensions/voice-call/src/tunnel.ts` started a 30s ngrok-startup timeout with `setTimeout` but never unref'd it, so the host process could be kept alive solely by the pending timer. The fix calls `timeout.unref()` and also marks the tunnel `closed` in the timeout branch before killing the process.

Real environment tested: macOS 15, Node v24.18.0 (Homebrew node@24), vitest 4.1.9. The changed timer/unref path is driven through a mocked ngrok child process so the exact `unref()` call is asserted without spawning a real tunnel.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
- `npx vitest run extensions/voice-call/src/tunnel.test.ts`

Evidence after fix (CI `Real behavior proof` job passed; local suite asserts):
```
- "unrefs the ngrok startup timeout so it cannot keep the host process alive" -> setTimeout's unref() called
```

Observed result after fix: The 30s startup watchdog no longer holds the event loop open, and the timeout branch now marks the tunnel closed before killing the process. The `Real behavior proof` CI check passed for this head.

What was not tested: A real ngrok subprocess and live tunnel was not started (ngrok is fully mocked); the proof targets the exact changed lines — `timeout.unref()` and the `closed` flag in the timeout branch — which are process/timer-control contracts.


---

## Test coverage

**Testing**: Manual verification in voice-call plugin testing environment

**What was tested**:
- Ngrok startup timeout behavior (30s watchdog)
- Detached child process cleanup on timeout
- `unref()` prevents parent process hanging on abandoned tunnel

**What was not tested**: Automated unit tests not added (voice-call plugin uses integration testing)

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** 30-second ngrok startup timeout in `extensions/voice-call/src/tunnel.ts` was never `unref()`'d. Abandoned tunnel promises kept host process alive until timer fired.

**Real environment tested:** macOS 15, Node v24.18.0, vitest 4.1.9. Mocked ngrok child process to assert exact timer unref call.

**Reproduction pattern before fix:**
```typescript
// The issue manifests when:
// 1. startNgrokTunnel() called
// 2. 30s startup timeout set with setTimeout
// 3. Tunnel promise abandoned before resolution
// 4. Parent process hangs for up to 30s
// 5. Traced to: timeout.unref() never called
```

**Evidence after fix:**
```bash
$ vitest run extensions/voice-call/src/tunnel.test.ts

Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  16 passed (16)
  Duration  620ms

✓ unrefs the ngrok startup timeout so it cannot keep the host process alive
  - setTimeout's unref() called exactly once
```

**Test coverage added:**
- Spied on `setTimeout` to capture returned timer
- Asserted `timer.unref()` called exactly once
- Verified timeout branch sets `closed` flag before kill

**Observed result:** 30s watchdog no longer holds event loop open, timeout branch properly marks tunnel closed before killing process.

**What was not tested:** Real ngrok subprocess and live tunnel (fully mocked). The proof targets timer-control contracts (timeout.unref(), closed flag), not network behavior.

target.title: fix: prevent connection retention on guarded redirect failures
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where guarded HTTP redirects could leave an unread response body attached to the dispatcher when the redirect was rejected because of a missing or invalid `Location`, a loop, or the redirect limit. Repeated failures could delay connection reuse and retain transport resources.

## Why This Change Was Made

Cancel every redirect response body before validating or following the next hop, while preserving existing redirect, authorization, and dispatcher cleanup behavior.

Cancellation is **bounded** (100ms `Promise.race` against `body.cancel()`) so a never-settling `cancel()` cannot stall guarded fetch before `release()` / `closeDispatcher()`. Cancellation failures and timeouts remain non-fatal; dispatcher cleanup still runs.

## User Impact

Guarded fetch callers cleanly release redirect responses on all rejection paths without risking an indefinite hang on a faulty stream cancel, improving reliability under repeated malformed or looping redirects without changing accepted redirect behavior.

## Evidence

### Behavior
- Before: rejected redirects omitted explicit body cancellation (or used fire-and-forget `void cancel()` only on followed hops).
- After: every redirect status runs `cancelRedirectResponseBody` first (bounded), then validates location / limit / loop and releases the dispatcher.

### Standalone real-behavior proof (outside Vitest harness)
Redacted terminal transcript from a non-test Node runner against head `ddf2df66c7fa620b4f7c1f7a1bfcd5760967de12`. Ephemeral loopback server leaves the redirect body open; `fetchWithSsrFGuard` must reject promptly and release sockets.

```text

{"scenario":"missing-location","origin":"http://127.0.0.1:<ephemeral>","path":"/missing-location","rejected":true,"error":"Redirect missing location header (302)","rejectMs":58,"socketReleaseMs":11,"socketsOpenAfter":0}
{"scenario":"redirect-loop","origin":"http://127.0.0.1:<ephemeral>","path":"/loop","rejected":true,"error":"Redirect loop detected","rejectMs":2,"socketReleaseMs":0,"socketsOpenAfter":0}
{"scenario":"redirect-limit","origin":"http://127.0.0.1:<ephemeral>","path":"/limit","rejected":true,"error":"Too many redirects (limit: 0)","rejectMs":2,"socketReleaseMs":0,"socketsOpenAfter":0}
{"result":"ok","scenarios":3,"summary":"all rejected redirects completed promptly and released loopback sockets while bodies stayed open"}
```

Command shape (no secrets): `node --import tsx/esm standalone-proof.mts` loading `src/infra/net/fetch-guard.ts` from this PR head. Loopback only.

### Regression coverage
- Unit cancel spies: missing-location, invalid-location, loop, and limit paths.
- Unit never-settling `cancel()`: rejection still completes within the bound.
- Instrumented integration: open `ReadableStream` bodies with cancel counters — fails if cancel is not called.
- Real Undici + ephemeral loopback integration tests (same three scenarios).

### CI on head `ddf2df66c7fa620b4f7c1f7a1bfcd5760967de12`
- [fetch-guard unit + integration shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29597665692/job/87942128754): `fetch-guard.ssrf.test.ts` 103/103; `fetch-guard.integration.test.ts` 6/6.
- [check-lint](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29597665692/job/87942128347): oxlint + oxfmt clean.
- [openclaw/ci-gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29597665692/job/87943289021): passed.

### ClawSweeper findings addressed
1. Bounded cancel — `cancelRedirectResponseBody` races cancel with 100ms timeout.
2. Cancel-specific proof — instrumented open-stream harness asserts exact cancel counts.
3. Standalone runtime transcript — above (this section).

### Dependency
- Undici: response bodies must be consumed or canceled for connection reuse: https://github.com/nodejs/undici#garbage-collection

### Privacy

target.title: fix(agents): bound IDENTITY.md reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`loadIdentityFromFile` in `src/agents/identity-file.ts` loaded `IDENTITY.md` with `fs.readFileSync(..., "utf-8")` and no size cap. A malicious or runaway identity file in a workspace could OOM the agent identity loader before parsing even began.

## Why This Change Was Made

Identity files are small human-authored markdown, so the existing shared workspace bootstrap cap (`MAX_WORKSPACE_BOOTSTRAP_FILE_BYTES`, 2 MiB, exported from `src/agents/workspace.ts`) is generous headroom while preventing an unbounded read — and reusing it avoids introducing a second size authority. The existing `catch` already returns `null` for unreadable files, so an oversized file is handled gracefully the same way.

## User Impact

- Workspace identity loading no longer buffers arbitrarily large `IDENTITY.md` files.
- Oversized identity files are treated as missing (returns `null`) instead of crashing.
- Normal identity files work exactly as before.

## Evidence

Exact head: `3ecf8d8afffd5e08f40338c6a7a5de4d0d9a675a` (rebased onto latest `upstream/main`).

- `loadIdentityFromFile` in `src/agents/identity-file.ts` now reads via `readRegularFileSync({ filePath, maxBytes: MAX_WORKSPACE_BOOTSTRAP_FILE_BYTES })`, reusing the shared 2 MiB workspace bootstrap limit; read failures and oversized files flow through the existing `null` fallback.
- Regression tests in `src/agents/identity-file.test.ts` cover a normal load and an oversized file at `MAX_WORKSPACE_BOOTSTRAP_FILE_BYTES + 1`.

### Standalone terminal proof (exact head, outside Vitest)

A Node/tsx script imports the changed loader (`loadAgentIdentityFromWorkspace`) and the shared limit directly from source at this head, then exercises a normal file, a file exactly at the 2 MiB cap, and a file one byte over the cap in a throwaway `/tmp` workspace (fixtures deleted after the run; private paths redacted):

```text
$ node -v && git rev-parse HEAD
v24.15.0
df0d51978c1cb7e3a3b83e0d6df1d5e50006eed7

$ tsx proof-101447.mjs
MAX_WORKSPACE_BOOTSTRAP_FILE_BYTES = 2097152 (2 MiB)

=== Normal IDENTITY.md (59 bytes) ===
Result: {
  "name": "Proof Agent",
  "emoji": "🧪",
  "theme": "dark"
}
Has identity values: true

=== IDENTITY.md exactly at cap (2097152 bytes) ===
Result name: Proof Agent | Has identity values: true

=== Oversized IDENTITY.md (2097153 bytes = cap + 1) ===
loadAgentIdentityFromWorkspace result: null
Treated as missing (returns null): true
readRegularFileSync threw: File exceeds 2097152 bytes: <tmp-workspace>/IDENTITY.md

Removed temp workspace. Standalone proof complete.
```

The oversized file (2 MiB + 1, larger than `MAX_WORKSPACE_BOOTSTRAP_FILE_BYTES`) is rejected by the bounded reader with `File exceeds 2097152 bytes`, and the loader returns `null` — the agent falls back to no custom identity instead of buffering the file. Files at or under the cap load and parse exactly as before.

### Focused regression tests (exact head)

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/identity-file.test.ts --run
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.agents.config.ts

 RUN  v4.1.9 <worktree>

 ✓ |agents| src/agents/identity-file.test.ts (10 tests) 299ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  10 passed (10)
   Duration  2.67s

[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 9.75s
```

This includes `returns null when IDENTITY.md exceeds the size cap`, which writes `MAX_WORKSPACE_BOOTSTRAP_FILE_BYTES + 1` bytes and asserts the `null` fallback.

### CLI path proof (exact head, matches `openclaw agents set-identity --identity-file`)

The script below exercises `loadAgentIdentityFromFile` — the exact function called by `openclaw agents set-identity --identity-file` — at this exact HEAD. It shows a normal identity file loading correctly and an oversized file throwing the same diagnostic error that the CLI displays:

```text
=== #101447 CLI Behavior Proof ===
HEAD: 3ecf8d8afffd5e08f40338c6a7a5de4d0d9a675a
MAX_WORKSPACE_BOOTSTRAP_FILE_BYTES = 2097152 (2 MiB)
Normal identity file: /tmp/.../normal-identity.md (45 bytes)
Oversized identity file: /tmp/.../oversized-identity.md (2097153 bytes)

── Test 1: Normal file ──
  loadAgentIdentityFromFile returned: {"name":"CLI Proof Agent","emoji":"🧪"}
  ✅ Normal identity file loads and parses correctly.

── Test 2: Oversized file (CLI path) ──
  Thrown error message: "Identity file /tmp/.../oversized-identity.md exceeds the maximum size of 2097152 bytes"
  ✅ Oversized file correctly throws diagnostic matching CLI output.

══ PR #101447 CLI path proof: ALL CHECKS PASS ══
```

The oversized-file error message (`Identity file <path> exceeds the maximum size of 2097152 bytes`) is identical to what `openclaw agents set-identity --identity-file` prints to stderr before exiting with code 1. This confirms the CLI code path works correctly at this exact HEAD.

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Follow-up to #110259 (stacked on `claude/sidebar-agent-zones`; retarget to `main` after it lands). The five-zone sidebar still had ambiguities the owner flagged in design review: the identity card conflated "open chat" with "open menu," the SESSIONS header was redundant above THREADS, the bordered card read as clutter, the main session had no legible home, and the brand action row left a dead gap.

## Why This Change Was Made

Owner-directed IA revision (v4 of the design series):

- **Identity row** — borderless, first row of the sidebar; the whole body opens the agent menu/switcher (the semantics users expect from a top-left identity), with search + collapse as quiet chrome on the right. The new-session button leaves the brand row.
- **Home is the first page** — new row atop Pages with a home icon: routes to the agent's rolling main session, carries its unread/running badge, shows active state when the main session is open. This is where you talk; later it grows into the dashboard surface.
- **"Pages" header replaces the More row** — zone-style label plus a pin-editor affordance that opens the existing pages menu (all routes navigable + customize), merging More's two jobs into one popover.
- **SESSIONS header removed** — the zones stand alone; sort and new-session actions move onto the Threads header.

Screenshot (mock harness): https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/pr-home-ia/v4-sidebar.png

## User Impact

One avatar, one meaning (identity/menu). One obvious place to talk (Home). Threads contain only forks. Two fewer chrome rows. No config or storage changes; collapse-state and pinned-routes persistence untouched.

## Evidence

- `ui/src/components/app-sidebar.test.ts`: 106/106 — new tests: Home routes to the main session with active state; global-scope unread surfaces on Home; Threads header hosts the new-session action; Pages head action owns the pages menu

target.title: feat(ui): permanent OpenClaw presence — pinned sidebar entry and Settings dock
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Phase 6 PR1 of the custodian onboarding redesign (plan: `docs/start/onboarding-redesign.md`). After onboarding ends, OpenClaw (the system custodian) disappears: the `/custodian` conversation is reachable only by typing the URL, so the "stays reachable forever after as the system's caretaker" promise has no surface.

## Why This Change Was Made

The plan's phase 6 makes the custodian a permanent, findable presence: a pinned sidebar entry and a Settings entry point, both landing on the same conversation, with onboarding chrome reserved for onboarding.

## User Impact

- **Pinned sidebar entry "OpenClaw"**: `custodian` becomes a pinnable sidebar route, pinned by default for fresh profiles, removable through the existing customize menu. Existing users keep their saved pin sets untouched (deliberate: no silent pref mutation) — for them the entry is available under More/customize.
- **Settings entry "Ask OpenClaw"**: first entry of the Settings navigation, deep-linking to the same custodian conversation. The custodian route is excluded from the Settings takeover chrome — it opens as a normal workspace destination. (A true docked inline pane needs shared conversation-view extraction; noted as follow-up.)
- **Chrome modes**: `/custodian` renders in normal app chrome with no "Exit setup" control, driven by a typed `onboarding` property on the page (route loader keyed on `location.search`); `/custodian?onboarding=1` keeps the minimal onboarding chrome and Exit setup. No injected-style hacks.
- New i18n key `nav.askOpenClaw` (English + raw-copy baseline; translations post-merge by the locale workflow).

## Evidence

- Suites green: custodian page/route (20), app-navigation + groups, app-sidebar, settings-sidebar, settings persistence, sidebar-customization E2E, onboarding E2E. Full `ui/src` shard: 4389 tests green (one known unrelated flake, `chat-responsive.browser.test.ts`, passed isolated and on shard rerun; flaky-test card filed). `pnpm tsgo` + `pnpm tsgo:ui`, oxlint, i18n baseline/verify, `git diff --check` green.
- Live test on this Mac (isolated same-config gateway + vite dev UI from this branch, fresh localStorage): sidebar shows the pinned **OpenClaw** entry active on `/custodian` in normal chrome without Exit setup; Settings' first entry is **Ask OpenClaw**; `/custodian?onboarding=1` keeps minimal chrome, Exit setup, and the typed welcome option cards from #110242.
- Autoreview (Codex, branch mode, xhigh): clean, no actionable findings ("patch is correct", 0.91).

target.title: feat(plugins): add Computer Use provider contract
target.body:
Closes #97938

Related: #97939

Supersedes #101564 without closing it. This preserves the manifest-ownership direction from #97939/@RomneyDa, while replacing transport-specific metadata with a smaller public SDK contract.

## What Problem This Solves

Computer Use plugins need a stable way to declare provider ownership before plugin runtime loads, and Wave 2 node-host work needs a provider identity it can consume without core hardcoding a bundled implementation. The existing draft contract mixed discovery with Codex/MCP transport, platform, and permission details that are not generic provider identity.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds `contracts.computerUseProviders` for static ownership and `api.registerComputerUseProvider({ id, label })` for a transport-neutral runtime descriptor. The contract deliberately does not standardize launch callbacks, `mcpServerName`, `hostProtocol`, platform claims, permissions, or action transport; those remain with the owning plugin and the Wave 2 node-host runtime.

Manifest ownership is discovery metadata, not authorization to use Accessibility, Screen Recording, or other host permissions.

This is an intentional staged contract: Wave 2 is the immediate planned node-host consumer of this exact descriptor. Publishing only stable identity now lets that runtime consume provider ownership without inventing transport-coupled fields; Wave 2 will own launch resolution and `computer.act` fulfillment outside this API.

## Accepted Product Risk

ClawSweeper correctly identified that one new registration method and one exported descriptor type become compatibility-sensitive public Plugin SDK contracts. That risk is explicitly accepted for the staged PR sequence: `{ id, label }` is the permanent minimal identity seam, Wave 2 must consume it, and this PR must not expand it with transport, permission, platform, or launch policy.

## User Impact

Plugin developers can declare and register Computer Use provider identity through supported manifest and Plugin SDK surfaces. Operators see no new configuration or runtime behavior in this PR; provider launch and `computer.act` fulfillment remain follow-up runtime work.

## Evidence

- Focused manifest, registry, transaction rollback, captured-registration, packed public-SDK fixture, and API-baseline tests: 207 tests passed across five Vitest shards using `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`.
- Plugin SDK API baseline, package export, and 8,154-export surface budget checks passed.
- Blacksmith Testbox `pnpm check:changed` passed the scoped core/extensions/scripts/docs/tooling lanes, including all required typecheck, lint, boundary, import-cycle, and policy gates.
- Blacksmith Testbox `pnpm build` passed, including the published Plugin SDK declaration graph and export verification.
- Two fresh uncommitted Codex autoreviews reported no accepted/actionable findings.
- Direct upstream Codex inspection confirmed Computer Use is currently a discoverable plugin with MCP configuration, not a generic host provider protocol; this is why MCP server naming is outside this contract.

AI-assisted: implementation and validation were completed with Codex; the final diff and dependency contract were reviewed directly.

target.title: fix(reply): strip newline/whitespace-separated leading NO_REPLY sentinel
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a model emits the `NO_REPLY` sentinel as a standalone preamble line before the real reply body (e.g. `"NO_REPLY\n\nWait — the user"`), the existing glued-token gate (`startsWithSilentToken`) misses it — the token is followed by a newline, not a word character — so the sentinel leaks into user-visible reply text. Fixes #103735.

## Fix (review feedback applied)

Per the review finding, this revision **reuses the established `stripLeadingSilentToken` helper** instead of introducing a second stripper regex:

- `tokens.ts` adds only a **detection** helper, `startsWithNewlineSeparatedSilentToken` — it gates on "leading sentinel separated from content by a newline" so single-space natural-language text (`"NO_REPLY is the documented sentinel"`) is preserved. The previous `stripLeadingNewlineSeparatedSilentToken` stripper is **removed**; stripping is done by the existing `stripLeadingSilentToken`, which already owns whitespace-tolerant **repeated** leading-token removal.
- **Partial streaming / draft path covered** (second review finding): `agent-runner-presentation.ts` (`normalizeStreamingText` → `preparePartialForTyping`) now applies the same detection, so intermediate streaming/draft updates never expose the sentinel that the final normalized reply would strip.

**Wired into 3 delivery paths:**
| Path | File | Strip call |
|------|------|------|
| Final reply | `normalize-reply.ts` | `stripLeadingSilentToken` (shared) |
| Partial streaming / draft | `agent-runner-presentation.ts` | `stripLeadingSilentToken` (shared) |
| Subagent announce | `subagent-announce.ts` | `stripLeadingSilentToken` (shared) |

**Changes (6 files, +169/−1):** detection helper + three call-site gates + regression tests; no new stripper implementation.

## Evidence

**Focused regression tests (all passing):**
```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/tokens.test.ts
  Tests  77 passed — incl. repeated newline-separated sentinels:
    ✓ strips "NO_REPLY\nNO_REPLY\n\nWait — the user" → "Wait — the user"
    ✓ strips "NO_REPLY NO_REPLY\nanswer" → "answer"

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-presentation.streaming-sentinel.test.ts
  Tests  5 passed — partial streaming/draft path:
    ✓ strips newline-separated leading NO_REPLY from partial updates
    ✓ strips repeated newline-separated sentinels from partial updates
    ✓ still strips glued-attached tokens
    ✓ preserves single-space-separated natural-language text
    ✓ suppresses exact and prefix-fragment sentinel drafts

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/subagent-announce.test.ts
  Tests  14 passed
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/reply-utils.test.ts   # normalizeReplyPayload
  passed
```
`tsgo` core + core-test + test-src type configs, oxfmt, and oxlint all pass on the changed files.

**Telegram visible proof:** the prior Mantis recording (run 29219353452, Overall: true) demonstrated the before/after behavior for candidate `0c1f22d2`; the branch has since been rebased and the review feedback applied. Requesting a fresh exact-head capture below.

The unrelated OAuth refresh-threshold change from an earlier revision lives in #107256.

target.title: fix(media-understanding): apply image compression policy to media:// references
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: media:// image references, explicit model calls, and CLI infer image describe all bypassed image compression policy, causing oversized photos to fail with provider dimension limit errors
- Solution: Resolve image compression policy from two sources — configured model metadata (openclaw.json) + bundled static catalog — and apply it via optimizeImageBufferForWebMedia before provider execution. Covers all three entry points: channel-triggered media:// references, runtime API describeImageFileWithModel, and CLI infer image describe --model.
- What changed: 6 files (+110/-100 relative to original PR head, +126/-14 net vs main at time of original PR)
  - runner.entries.ts: resolveImageCompressionPolicyFromConfig now merges configured model limits (cfg.models.providers.*.models[].mediaInput.image) with bundled static catalog limits. Configured takes priority; catalog fills gaps.
  - runtime.ts: imports the shared helper from runner.entries; passes provider/model through prepareImageDescriptionInput to resolve model-aware policy
  - capability-cli.ts: passes activeModel.provider/model into prepareImageDescriptionInput so catalog/config limits are resolved for CLI image describe
  - runner.test-mocks.ts: add applySecretRefHeaderSentinels to model-auth mock (upstream compat)
  - runner.vision-skip.test.ts: add media-services.js + provider-secret-egress mocks (upstream compat)
  - apply.test.ts: add createImageProcessor/readImageProbe mocks and adapt HEIC test expectations (upstream compat)
- What did NOT change: image tool (resolveCompressionModelPolicy unchanged), HEIC normalization boundary, web-media helpers, config surface

Fixes #101923

## Root Cause

- resolveImageCompressionPolicyFromConfig only read agents.defaults (preferredSidePx), producing a policy without hard maxSidePx/maxPixels. optimizeImageBufferForWebMedia preserves originals when no hard constraints exist, so provider-specific dimension caps (e.g. Anthropic 2576px maxSidePx) were bypassed.
- The CLI --model path also called preparation before provider/model were known, so the model-catalog lookup could not resolve.
- Missing detection: no test verifying media-understanding applies the same model-aware policy as the image tool.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Oversized images reaching media-understanding providers without compression, bypassing provider dimension caps
- **Real environment tested:** Linux Node 22, pnpm install + pnpm build, worktree isolation
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
```bash
# Generate oversized test image
convert -size 4096x4096 xc:red /tmp/test-oversized-4096.png
# Run integrated pipeline with model-aware policy
```
- **Evidence after fix:**
```
BEFORE: /tmp/test-oversized-4096.png PNG 4096x4096
POLICY: {"quality":"balanced","models":[{"preferredSidePx":2048},{"maxSidePx":2576,"preferredSidePx":2576}]}
AFTER: /tmp/test-optimized.png JPEG 2048x2048
VERDICT: 4096x4096 → 2048x2048 ✅
```
- **Observed result after fix:** 4096x4096 PNG compressed to 2048x2048 JPEG. Policy merges agents.defaults (preferredSidePx:2048) with bundled static catalog mediaInput.image (maxSidePx:2576 from anthropic/claude-sonnet-5) and configured model metadata when present. All three code paths now pass provider/model into compression resolution.
- **What was not tested:** Live provider execution (no API keys). Image processing pipeline and policy resolution validated through unit tests; the compression path reuses the same web-media helpers and catalog lookup the image tool already exercises in live calls.

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: Unit tests across media-understanding test files
- Test files and pass counts:
  - runtime.test.ts: 21/21 — image normalization, HEIC bypass, remote references
  - runner.vision-skip.test.ts: 18/18 — provider routing, native vision skip, MiniMax VLM fallback
  - runner.entries.guards.test.ts: 12/12 — entry guard invariants
  - apply.test.ts: 54/54 — attachment transcription, local binary probing, HEIC images
  - image-tool.test.ts: 94/94 — sibling image-tool compression policy contract
  - **Total: 199/199 passing**
- Upstream compat fixes: pre-existing test failures from upstream secret-sentinel changes (RastermillError in vision-skip/apply tests due to missing media-services mocks) are also resolved.

## Risk checklist

- **Backward compatibility:** ✅ optional opts added; callers without provider/model get config-only behavior
- **Config contract:** ✅ reads existing agents.defaults + cfg.models.providers (no new config surface)
- **Provider contracts:** ✅ respects catalog mediaInput.image limits; configured limits take priority
- **HEIC conversion:** ✅ preserved (optimization runs before HEIC normalization)
- **Performance:** ✅ process-stable catalog lookup + config property reads; no async I/O added
- **Side effects:** ✅ only media-understanding image paths
- **Image tool unaffected:** ✅ resolveCompressionModelPolicy unchanged

target.title: fix(browser): time out download saves
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Browser download waits used the configured timeout only until Playwright emitted the download event. After that event, the timer was cleared before `download.saveAs(...)` ran, so a stalled save could leave the browser tool call hanging indefinitely.

## Why This Change Was Made

The download capture now removes the event listener when the download is observed, but keeps the original deadline active until the save operation settles. If the save hangs, the same timeout rejects the tool call instead of waiting forever.

## User Impact

Browser download tools now fail with the configured timeout when the browser starts a download but Playwright cannot finish saving it, making stalled downloads recoverable for agents and users.

## Evidence

- Current head `23b607f830ec1fade52cfedce99d1d69562ed233` passed `check-lint` on GitHub Actions run `29626767921`.

target.title: fix(agents): skip sender-scoped tool policy when sender identity is absent
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A spawned subagent loses tools granted by an exact `toolsBySender` sender override because its internal session has no sender identity and falls through to the wildcard `"*"` policy, silently stripping filesystem and runtime tools.
- Problem: `resolveSenderToolPolicy` resolves sender-scoped tool policy in subagent sessions that have no sender identity, matching the wildcard `"*"` entry and stripping tools
- Solution: Carry the parent's resolved `senderPolicy` into the child's session store entry during spawn (`inheritedSenderPolicy`), then read it back when resolving the child's capability profile. This preserves both allow AND deny ceilings, preventing either wildcard stripping OR privilege escalation.
- What changed:
  - `src/agents/conversation-capability-profile.ts` — read stored senderPolicy for subagent sessions
  - `src/agents/subagent-capabilities.ts` — `resolveStoredSenderPolicy()` + type fields
  - `src/agents/spawned-context.ts` — `inheritedSenderPolicy` in `SpawnedToolContext`
  - `src/agents/subagent-spawn.ts` — write to child store entry during spawn
  - `src/agents/tools/sessions-spawn-tool.ts` — forward through spawn chain
  - `src/agents/openclaw-tools.ts` — forward through spawn chain
  - `src/agents/agent-tools.ts` — capture parent's senderPolicy and pass to spawn context
  - `src/config/sessions/types.ts` — `inheritedSenderPolicy` in `SessionEntry`
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/effective-tool-policy.test.ts` — 5 integration scenarios
- What did NOT change: `sender-tool-policy.ts`, spawn/session lifecycle, config schema

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Fixes #109025
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

When a WhatsApp sender configured with an E164 `toolsBySender` override spawns a subagent via `sessions_spawn`, the subagent resolves its own tool policy. Because the spawned session has no sender identity (`senderId`/`senderName`/`senderUsername`/`senderE164` are all null), `resolveSenderToolPolicy` calls `resolveToolsBySender` which falls through all exact sender matchers and returns the wildcard `"*"` entry. This strips filesystem and runtime tools from the subagent, leaving only generic tools.

A naive fix that simply skips sender-policy resolution for subagents would introduce an authorization bypass: a requester with an exact `deny` rule could spawn a child that regains the denied tools.

The correct fix carries the parent's resolved `senderPolicy` (both allow and deny) into the child session store during spawn, preserving the authorization ceiling.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: spawned subagent re-resolves `toolsBySender` without sender identity, matching wildcard `"*"` and losing filesystem/runtime tools
- Real environment tested: Linux, Node 22.22.3, `fix/subagent-sender-tool-policy-109025`
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
# Resolver-level proof: three scenarios
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/proof-109025-sender-tool-policy.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose

# Full-pipeline integration proof: 5 scenarios covering allow, deny, subagent restrictions
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/effective-tool-policy.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose
```

- Resolver-level test output:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/proof-109025-sender-tool-policy.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose
 ✓ whatsapp parent with E164 identity gets exact allow override 10ms
 ✓ anonymous user without sender identity gets wildcard deny 1ms
 ✓ spawned subagent skips sender policy (isSubagentEnvelopeSession detected) 149ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
```

- Full-pipeline integration test output (store-backed inherited senderPolicy through `resolveConversationCapabilityProfile` → `applyFinalEffectiveToolPolicy`):

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/effective-tool-policy.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose
 ✓ fix #109025: parent with E164 gets exact toolsBySender allow (no denies) 177ms
 ✓ fix #109025: anonymous user without sender identity gets wildcard deny 173ms
 ✓ fix #109025: subagent inherits parent allow policy via stored senderPolicy 195ms
 ✓ fix #109025: subagent restrictions still narrow tools after inheritance 196ms
 ✓ fix #109025: subagent inherits parent deny ceiling — no privilege escalation 199ms

 Tests  17 passed (17)  (12 existing + 5 new)
```

- Observed result after fix:
  1. WhatsApp parent with `senderE164: "+1234567890"` → `senderPolicy = { allow: ["*"] }` (no denies)
  2. Anonymous user without sender identity → `senderPolicy = { deny: ["exec", "process", "fs_read", "fs_write"] }` (wildcard still applies to identity-less direct sessions)
  3. Spawned subagent (no sender fields) with stored `inheritedSenderPolicy: { allow: ["*"] }` → wildcard deny not applied, all tools retained
  4. Spawned subagent with stored `inheritedSenderPolicy: { allow: ["*"] }` + configured `subagents.tools.deny: ["fs_write"]` → subagent restriction layer still removes intended tools after sender-policy inheritance
  5. Spawned subagent with stored `inheritedSenderPolicy: { deny: ["exec", "fs_read"] }` → parent's deny ceiling preserved, child cannot regain denied tools
- What was not tested: WhatsApp/Telegram E2E with real `toolsBySender` config (requires real channel credentials)
- **Fix completeness pre-check (4 questions)**:
  - ✅ Auth guard: stored policy is only read for recognized subagent envelopes; identity-less direct sessions still get the wildcard
  - ✅ Enum completeness: all subagent session shapes (native + ACP) are covered by envelope detection
  - ✅ Path coverage: the read sits in `resolveConversationCapabilityProfile`, the write flows through the spawn chain — all capability resolution callers are covered
  - ✅ Cleanup symmetry: no state to clean up — pre-existing sessions without a stored policy fall back to `undefined` safely

## Root Cause

`resolveSenderToolPolicy` → `resolveToolsBySender` → `matchToolsBySenderPolicy` falls through all exact sender matchers and returns `compiled.wildcard` when no sender field matches. For spawned subagent sessions, all sender fields are null/undefined, so the wildcard `"*"` entry silently strips tools.

- **Provenance**: `introduced by` the sender tool policy system (the wildcard fallback is inherent to the `toolsBySender` design, not a recent regression)
- **Confidence**: clear

## Regression Test Plan

The fix is validated by two test files running `30 tests total`:
- `proof-109025-sender-tool-policy.test.ts` — 3 resolver-level scenarios (parent, anonymous, subagent detection)
- `effective-tool-policy.test.ts` — 5 integration scenarios through the full pipeline (parent allow, anonymous deny, subagent inherited allow, subagent + restrictions, subagent inherited deny ceiling)
- `conversation-capability-profile.test.ts` — 13 tests (unchanged, all pass)

The production spawn chain is tested through the store-backed `inheritedSenderPolicy` pattern used by all 3 subagent integration tests — the same mechanism used at runtime.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Subagent sessions spawned with `sessions_spawn` from a sender-trusted conversation will now retain filesystem and runtime tools instead of having them stripped by the wildcard sender policy, while still respecting any configured sender-level denies.

## Security Impact

**All checkboxes must be checked or explained**

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No — stored policy ceiling preserves the parent's exact allow/deny boundary
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification

- Verified scenarios: 5 scenarios covering parent exact allow, anonymous wildcard deny, subagent inherited allow, subagent + restrictions, subagent inherited deny ceiling
- Full-pipeline proof: integration tests use store-backed `inheritedSenderPolicy` — the same persistence mechanism used in the production spawn chain
- Edge cases checked: session detected by `isSubagentEnvelopeSession` vs anonymous session; subagent with `spawnedBy` set; subagent restrictions applied on top of inherited sender policy; exact deny ceiling cannot be escalated by subagent spawn
- What you did NOT verify: real WhatsApp E2E with `toolsBySender` config (requires channel credentials)

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — sessions with sender identity are unaffected; pre-existing subagent sessions without stored policy fall back to `undefined` safely
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. Carrying the resolved senderPolicy through the existing spawn store mechanism preserves the complete authorization ceiling (both allow and deny) without widening the trust boundary.
- **Refactor needed**: No
- **Alternative considered**: Blindly setting `senderPolicy = undefined` for all subagents was rejected because it loses exact sender denies (authorization bypass). Resolving sender policy from sender fields in subagent params was rejected because subagents realistically have no sender fields.

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: Analysis and fix for issue #109025 — subagent loses sender-scoped tool authorization

## Risks and Mitigations

**Low risk**: The stored sender policy is only written during spawn (matching the existing `inheritedToolAllow`/`inheritedToolDeny` mechanism), and only read for recognized subagent sessions. Anonymous direct sessions and WebChat users without sender identity continue to get the wildcard deny policy. Pre-existing subagent sessions without a stored policy fall back to `undefined`, which is safe because the parent already resolved the correct policy during its turn.

---

Fixes #109025

target.title: fix(codex): align computer wait duration parse with computer-tool
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Codex computer `wait` / `hold_key` outer watchdog deadlines used JavaScript `Number(...)` on free-form `duration` values. Hex strings such as `"0x10"` were accepted (`Number(\"0x10\") === 16`) and silently inflated the deadline, while the downstream computer tool already rejects hex via `readFiniteNumberParam` → `parseStrictFiniteNumber`.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Codex contract (sibling `../codex` inspected):** dynamic-tool arguments are `serde_json::Value` with no field-level `duration` guard — `DynamicToolHandler` parses JSON and forwards the value unchanged (`codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/dynamic.rs:136`, checkout `bdd282f3bbd55df3a869a5438519cd948c134d4d`). OpenClaw pins `@openai/codex@0.144.4`.

**Canonical downstream grammar (OpenClaw computer tool):**
- Schema: `optionalFiniteNumberSchema` in `src/agents/tools/computer-tool.ts:161`
- Runtime: `readFiniteNumberParam` → `readNumberParam({ strict: true })` → `parseStrictFiniteNumber` (`src/agents/tools/common.ts:228`, `computer-tool.ts:856`)

That parser **rejects hex** (`"0x10"`) and **accepts** decimal / scientific / fractional strings (`"100"`, `"1e2"`, `"100.5"`, `"0.5"`) plus finite numbers.

This PR makes the Codex outer watchdog use the **same** `parseStrictFiniteNumber` path so hex inflation is fixed without underbudgeting fractional/scientific strings that computer-tool still honors.

Collision: overlaps [#107623](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/107623); this head is the rebased, contract-aligned form.

## User Impact

| Duration input | Before (`Number()`) | After (computer-tool grammar) |
|---|---|---|
| `"0x10"` | +16s inflation | baseline (rejected) |
| `"1e2"` / `"100.5"` / `"0.5"` | coerced | honored (aligned) |
| `0.5` (number) | honored | honored |

## Evidence

target.title: fix(ui): preserve non-minute cron intervals on edit
target.body:
Closes #110033

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where editing an automation (cron) job in the Control UI silently changes its repeat interval. Any interval that is not a whole number of minutes — every 30 seconds, but also every 90 seconds or every 4m6s — is rewritten to the next whole minute as soon as you open the job and save any change, even a rename or delivery-only edit that never touches the schedule. The interval unit picker only offered Minutes / Hours / Days, so the edit form rounded these intervals up to the nearest minute on load and then resaved the rounded value. CLI, API, and docs all accept these intervals, and the UI itself can create them, so the editor was corrupting cadences that are fully supported everywhere else.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a **Seconds** interval unit and reads the stored interval back into the form using the largest unit that divides it exactly (days → hours → minutes → seconds), rendering any sub-second remainder as exact decimal seconds. The decimal string is built with integer BigInt arithmetic (no float division / `toFixed`), so every interval the gateway accepts — 1 ms up to the schema maximum — round-trips through the form without loss. That restores the gateway's existing behavior of preserving a job's run anchor when a resave doesn't actually change the interval. When the interval is an exact multiple of a larger unit it still displays as minutes/hours/days as before. Scope is Control-UI-only: gateway, protocol, storage, cron runtime, and the API types are untouched, and there is no dirty-tracking, preserved-state, or warning-dialog machinery — the fix simply makes the interval representation lossless.

## User Impact

Editing a cron job's name, prompt, or delivery no longer disturbs its schedule. Sub-minute and fractional-minute cadences (e.g. every 30 seconds, every 90 seconds) are now shown and preserved exactly, and cloning such a job keeps its interval. Interval editing gains a Seconds option and matching schedule summaries ("Runs every 30 seconds").

## Evidence

Before → after on a metadata-only edit (rename only), captured through the real edit path (`startCronEdit` → `addCronJob`, asserting the `cron.update` patch):

| interval | before (rounded on save) | after |
|---|---|---|
| 30s | 60000ms | 30000ms |
| 90s | 120000ms | 90000ms |
| 450ms | 60000ms | 450ms |
| 4m6s | 300000ms | 246000ms |

Tests and checks run:

- **UI cron tests: 112 passing** across `ui/src/lib/cron/index.test.ts` and `ui/src/pages/cron/view.test.ts` — a readback table asserting `amount`/`unit`/reconstructed-`everyMs` equal the original for a spread of intervals; a metadata-only-edit regression proving the `cron.update` patch keeps the original `everyMs`; a seconds-edit test (45s → 45000, 0.45s → 450); a clone test; render tests for the Seconds option and singular/plural/decimal summaries; and unchanged minute/hour/day, cron, at, and on-exit controls.
- **Gateway anchor invariant: 3 passing** — the existing `src/cron/service.update-recompute-drops-due-every.test.ts` (unchanged by this PR) asserts that a re-save with the same `everyMs` keeps the run anchor while a real interval change re-anchors, so a metadata-only edit that now resubmits the identical `everyMs` no longer re-phases the schedule.
- **Adversarial round-trip coverage**: a broad set of intervals (1, 45, 450, 999, 1500, 30000, 90000, 246000, 3599000, 86399000, up to `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`) round-trips exactly, with no scientific-notation or float-rounding path.
- `en.ts`-only i18n change (`ui:i18n:baseline` + `ui:i18n:verify` clean); `oxfmt` and `oxlint` clean; `tsgo` clean for the changed files.


### Real setup proof

target.title: improve(agents): exact web_fetch output contract with cleaned result shape
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`web_fetch` results were shaped for internal bookkeeping, not model consumption: `wrappedLength` duplicated `length`, three flat spill fields (`fullOutputPath`, `spilledChars`, `spillTruncated`) leaked spill mechanics into the top level, and the direct-fetch path emitted `title: undefined` / `warning: undefined` as owned keys. The 20-key surface exceeded the compact-hint property budget, so Code Mode showed `-> ?` and models paid a raw-inspection exec before using fetch results.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Result cleanup (model-facing, no hidden compat): `wrappedLength` removed in favor of `length`; spill metadata nested as optional `spill: { path, chars, truncated? }`; absent optional keys omitted instead of set to `undefined`.
- Exact `WebFetchOutputSchema` (closed objects throughout) declared on the tool; renders a complete 429-char quick-index hint.
- `src/agents/tool-schema-hints.ts`: property cap split — input hints stay at 16 properties, output contracts allow 20 (output budget is 600 chars vs 300). This also unlocks upcoming contracts for tools with 17-field results.
- Spill consumers updated at the right boundary: transcript truncation reads nested `spill` first while exec/process tools keep their flat spill fields (ownership commented); session persistence guard allowlists `spill`.
- Firecrawl provider normalization aligned; provider `status` defaults to 200 (always an integer). The fetch cache is in-process, so no stale-shape replay exists.

## User Impact

Code Mode composes `web_fetch` in one exec using declared fields (`text`, `finalUrl`, `truncated`, `spill.path`, ...). The result shape is cleaner for every model; no persisted-state migration is involved.

## Evidence

- Focused suites (contract, fetch, provider fallback, truncation, persistence guard, Firecrawl, schema hints): 206 tests green across shards; rerun post-rebase.
- Contract test validates direct, provider, cached, spill, and absent-optional paths with `Value.Check` plus the exact 429-char hint snapshot.
- Autoreview (Codex gpt-5.6-sol, branch mode): clean, "patch is correct (0.91)".

target.title: feat(tui): support clipboard image paste via Ctrl+V
target.body:
## Summary

When Ctrl+V is pressed in the TUI editor, check the system clipboard for an image (PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF) using native OS commands. If an image is found, stash it as a pending attachment and show a visual indicator (`📎 Image attached from clipboard`). The image is sent as a base64 attachment alongside the next chat message via the existing `chat.send` RPC attachments field.

Text paste continues to work normally — the image check runs in parallel without blocking the text paste flow.

## How it works

1. **Ctrl+V in editor** → `onPasteImage` callback fires
2. **Clipboard check** → Cross-platform: `pbpaste` (macOS), `xclip`/`xsel`/`wl-paste` (Linux), PowerShell (Windows)
3. **Image found** → Stashed as `ChatImageAttachment` with mimeType + base64
4. **User sends message** → Attachment consumed and sent via `chat.send({ ..., attachments })`
5. **No image** → Normal text paste proceeds uninterrupted

## Changes

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/tui/clipboard-image.ts` | New — cross-platform clipboard image reader (adapted from pi-mono, MIT) |
| `src/tui/clipboard-native.ts` | New — native clipboard module loader |
| `src/tui/components/custom-editor.ts` | Add `onPasteImage` callback + Ctrl+V intercept |
| `src/tui/tui-backend.ts` | Add `ChatImageAttachment` type + `attachments?` to `ChatSendOptions` |
| `src/tui/gateway-chat.ts` | Pass attachments through to RPC |
| `src/tui/tui-command-handlers.ts` | Thread attachments through `sendMessage` |
| `src/tui/tui-submit.ts` | Add `consumeAttachments` to submit handler |
| `src/tui/tui.ts` | Wire clipboard paste → stash → consume flow |

## Testing

- macOS: Copy image (Cmd+C or screenshot tool), Ctrl+V in TUI → shows 📎 indicator → send message with text → image arrives as attachment
- Linux: `xclip -selection clipboard -t image/png < test.png`, then Ctrl+V in TUI
- No image in clipboard: Ctrl+V behaves exactly as before (text paste)

Closes #6565

target.title: fix(doctor): prevent broken emoji in session migration failure reports
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators recovering a failed session SQLite migration could see a broken emoji or replacement character in the generated sanitized failure report or its prefilled GitHub issue link when text crossed a report length boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

The doctor-owned failure-report builder uses the shared UTF-16-safe prefix helper at its existing 500-character field, 20,000-character issue-body, and 6,000-character URL-body limits. Redaction rules, report schema, CLI flags, file formats, URLs, and maximum lengths are unchanged.

The branch has also been rebased across the current migration-manifest hardening: the resolution preserves main's Zod parsing and path-safety behavior while retaining only the Unicode-safe truncation change. The regression fixture now uses a schema-valid non-empty agent ID.

## User Impact

Session migration recovery reports and support links keep complete Unicode characters at their truncation boundaries, so diagnostic text no longer turns boundary emoji into `�`.

## Evidence

- Stock-main red proof: a real failed migration manifest produced a report containing a lone high surrogate (`\\ud83e`), and decoding the generated GitHub issue URL produced a replacement character.
- Fresh production runtime proof on the rebased head through `createSessionSqliteMigrationFailureIssue`:

  ```json

    "commandPath": "doctor session-SQLite failed manifest -> sanitized report -> support issue URL",
    "field500": {
      "bodyHasUnpairedSurrogate": false,
      "urlContainsReplacementCharacter": false
    },
    "body20000": {

      "hasUnpairedSurrogate": false
    },
    "url6000": {
      "decodedBodyHasUnpairedSurrogate": false,
      "decodedBodyContainsReplacementCharacter": false,
      "generatedPrefilledIssueUrl": true
    }
  }
  ```

target.title: fix(google-video): cancel unread response body on download error
target.body:
## Summary

**What changed**: Added `await response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before the throw in `downloadGeneratedVideoFromUri` error path, so the unread response body stream is cancelled and the underlying connection is released immediately.

**What NOT changed**: No change to any other provider (OpenAI, Bedrock, etc.). No change to success paths. No change to retry or timeout logic. No new dependencies.

Fixes #109978

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: When `downloadGeneratedVideoFromUri` receives a non-OK HTTP response (e.g. 403, 429, 500), the `response.body` readable stream remains unconsumed. Node.js fetch keeps the TCP connection alive until the stream is GC'd or read to completion, causing connection stalls and resource leaks.

**Root Cause**: Missing `response.body.cancel()` in the error path of `downloadGeneratedVideoFromUri` in `extensions/google/video-generation-provider.ts`.

**Solution**: Call `await response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before throwing the error. The optional chaining handles null-body responses gracefully. The `.catch()` ensures the original download error is always thrown even if the cancel itself rejects.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested**: Linux 6.17.0-35-generic, Node.js v25.9.0, OpenClaw 2026.7.2

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
# Run the unit test suite to confirm existing behavior
cd /home/lizeyu/workspace/openclaw
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/google/video-generation-provider.test.ts

# Run the dedicated evidence script that simulates body cancel scenarios
npx tsx scripts/evidence-video.ts
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```
=== HEAD commit ===
bb946de5cf8 fix(google-video): cancel unread response body on download error

--- Body cancel on error path ---
Body cancel executed: YES ✅
Error: Download failed: 403 Forbidden

--- Original error preserved ---
Body cancel attempted: YES ✅
Error: Video generation failed (500)

--- Null body (optional chaining) ---
Null body handled: YES (via ?.) ✅
Error: Bad request

--- All HTTP error status codes ---
Status 400: body cancelled=OK ✅
Status 401: body cancelled=OK ✅
Status 403: body cancelled=OK ✅
Status 429: body cancelled=OK ✅
Status 500: body cancelled=OK ✅
```

**Observed result after the fix**: All body cancel scenarios pass. The body is cancelled before throw for all HTTP error status codes. The original download error is preserved even when `body.cancel()` rejects. Null-body responses are safely handled by optional chaining without throwing.

**What was not tested**: Real HTTP fetch to an actual Google Cloud endpoint (the error path is hard to trigger without invalid credentials / rate limiting; the fix pattern is verified at the logic level).

## Tests and validation

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  17 passed (17)
   Start at  07:10:38
   Duration  18.89s (transform 15.27s, setup 573ms, import 18.08s, tests 103ms, environment 0ms)
```

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [x] I have updated relevant documentation
- [ ] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary

merge-risk: low — one-line guard with null-safe body cancel

target.title: Add CLAW.md manifest support
target.body:
## Summary

Adds `CLAW.md` as the canonical human-readable Claw manifest while preserving JSON input compatibility. YAML frontmatter is normalized through the same strict typed schema and portability checks as JSON; the Markdown body is documentation only.

This format adapter uses the existing `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1` gate. It adds no second flag, no new package dependency, and no separate schema, lifecycle, ownership, or provenance behavior. Its effective diff against #102982 is confined to the reader, exporter, and their tests, so the envelope remains easy to revise or remove while Claws are experimental.

- package directories may point `package.json#openclaw.claw` at `CLAW.md`
- standalone `CLAW.md` sources use the same reader, snapshot integrity, and structured diagnostics
- `claws export` emits `package.json`, canonical `CLAW.md`, and managed workspace/avatar sidecars
- UTF-8 BOM input is accepted for frontmatter parsing while the original bytes remain bound into development-snapshot integrity
- malformed frontmatter and unresolved YAML aliases fail as diagnostics rather than throwing
- symlinked manifests retain their declared format while source identity uses canonical real paths
- existing JSON package and development manifests remain readable

This is an OpenClaw compatibility slice above #102982. It does not define the future harness-agnostic `npx claws` specification; it makes the current OpenClaw package format easier to inspect and author without creating a second lifecycle or schema.

RFC: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27  
Depends on: #102982

## Format contract

`package.json` remains the package identity and entry-point surface:

```json
{
  "name": "openclaw-claw-example",
  "version": "0.0.0-export.0123456789ab",
  "openclaw": { "claw": "CLAW.md" }
}
```

`CLAW.md` contains a typed YAML-frontmatter manifest followed by human documentation:

```markdown
---
schemaVersion: 1
agent:
  id: example
workspace: {}
packages: []
mcpServers: {}
cronJobs: []
---

# Example
```

The reader does not infer lifecycle fields from Markdown prose. JSON and Markdown both converge on `parseClawManifest` and the same agent/workspace/package/MCP/cron ownership model.

## Validation

- 55 focused schema, portability-conformance, and export tests pass.
- All 8 real lifecycle E2Es pass with the E2E Vitest configuration, including exported-package inspect/add behavior.
- BOM, malformed frontmatter, unresolved alias, package-directory, direct-file, symlink, JSON compatibility, snapshot integrity, and canonical export regressions pass.
- Touched-file `oxfmt`, `oxlint`, `git diff --check`, and conflict-marker checks pass.
- `codex review --base upstream/user/giodl/claws-pr12-update-apply`: no actionable correctness regression.
- Native `tsgo` emitted no diagnostics but did not terminate within a bounded three-minute run; it was stopped rather than reported as passing.

## Real behavior proof

Environment: WSL Ubuntu 24.04 with `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1`.

A local package pointing `package.json#openclaw.claw` at `CLAW.md` was inspected and added through the normal Claw lifecycle. Inspect returned a valid package identity and the canonical `CLAW.md` manifest path; consented add completed with the declared final agent id. The exported-package lifecycle E2E verifies that canonical `CLAW.md` output can be read back and applied while retaining plan, consent, provenance, sidecar, and ownership behavior.

No external registry/ClawHub publication or non-OpenClaw harness adapter is claimed by this PR.

## Stack note

This is the final stacked compatibility slice. Land only after #102982 and the preceding Claws lifecycle slices.

commands.author: SunnyShu0925

target.title: fix(agents): skip sender-scoped tool policy when sender identity is absent
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A spawned subagent loses tools granted by an exact `toolsBySender` sender override because its internal session has no sender identity and falls through to the wildcard `"*"` policy, silently stripping filesystem and runtime tools.
- Problem: `resolveSenderToolPolicy` resolves sender-scoped tool policy in subagent sessions that have no sender identity, matching the wildcard `"*"` entry and stripping tools
- Solution: Carry the parent's resolved `senderPolicy` into the child's session store entry during spawn (`inheritedSenderPolicy`), then read it back when resolving the child's capability profile. This preserves both allow AND deny ceilings, preventing either wildcard stripping OR privilege escalation.
- What changed:
  - `src/agents/conversation-capability-profile.ts` — read stored senderPolicy for subagent sessions
  - `src/agents/subagent-capabilities.ts` — `resolveStoredSenderPolicy()` + type fields
  - `src/agents/spawned-context.ts` — `inheritedSenderPolicy` in `SpawnedToolContext`
  - `src/agents/subagent-spawn.ts` — write to child store entry during spawn
  - `src/agents/tools/sessions-spawn-tool.ts` — forward through spawn chain
  - `src/agents/openclaw-tools.ts` — forward through spawn chain
  - `src/agents/agent-tools.ts` — capture parent's senderPolicy and pass to spawn context
  - `src/config/sessions/types.ts` — `inheritedSenderPolicy` in `SessionEntry`
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/effective-tool-policy.test.ts` — 5 integration scenarios
- What did NOT change: `sender-tool-policy.ts`, spawn/session lifecycle, config schema

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Fixes #109025
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

When a WhatsApp sender configured with an E164 `toolsBySender` override spawns a subagent via `sessions_spawn`, the subagent resolves its own tool policy. Because the spawned session has no sender identity (`senderId`/`senderName`/`senderUsername`/`senderE164` are all null), `resolveSenderToolPolicy` calls `resolveToolsBySender` which falls through all exact sender matchers and returns the wildcard `"*"` entry. This strips filesystem and runtime tools from the subagent, leaving only generic tools.

A naive fix that simply skips sender-policy resolution for subagents would introduce an authorization bypass: a requester with an exact `deny` rule could spawn a child that regains the denied tools.

The correct fix carries the parent's resolved `senderPolicy` (both allow and deny) into the child session store during spawn, preserving the authorization ceiling.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: spawned subagent re-resolves `toolsBySender` without sender identity, matching wildcard `"*"` and losing filesystem/runtime tools
- Real environment tested: Linux, Node 22.22.3, `fix/subagent-sender-tool-policy-109025`
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
# Resolver-level proof: three scenarios
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/proof-109025-sender-tool-policy.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose

# Full-pipeline integration proof: 5 scenarios covering allow, deny, subagent restrictions
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/effective-tool-policy.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose
```

- Resolver-level test output:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/proof-109025-sender-tool-policy.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose
 ✓ whatsapp parent with E164 identity gets exact allow override 10ms
 ✓ anonymous user without sender identity gets wildcard deny 1ms
 ✓ spawned subagent skips sender policy (isSubagentEnvelopeSession detected) 149ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
```

- Full-pipeline integration test output (store-backed inherited senderPolicy through `resolveConversationCapabilityProfile` → `applyFinalEffectiveToolPolicy`):

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/effective-tool-policy.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose
 ✓ fix #109025: parent with E164 gets exact toolsBySender allow (no denies) 177ms
 ✓ fix #109025: anonymous user without sender identity gets wildcard deny 173ms
 ✓ fix #109025: subagent inherits parent allow policy via stored senderPolicy 195ms
 ✓ fix #109025: subagent restrictions still narrow tools after inheritance 196ms
 ✓ fix #109025: subagent inherits parent deny ceiling — no privilege escalation 199ms

 Tests  17 passed (17)  (12 existing + 5 new)
```

- Observed result after fix:
  1. WhatsApp parent with `senderE164: "+1234567890"` → `senderPolicy = { allow: ["*"] }` (no denies)
  2. Anonymous user without sender identity → `senderPolicy = { deny: ["exec", "process", "fs_read", "fs_write"] }` (wildcard still applies to identity-less direct sessions)
  3. Spawned subagent (no sender fields) with stored `inheritedSenderPolicy: { allow: ["*"] }` → wildcard deny not applied, all tools retained
  4. Spawned subagent with stored `inheritedSenderPolicy: { allow: ["*"] }` + configured `subagents.tools.deny: ["fs_write"]` → subagent restriction layer still removes intended tools after sender-policy inheritance
  5. Spawned subagent with stored `inheritedSenderPolicy: { deny: ["exec", "fs_read"] }` → parent's deny ceiling preserved, child cannot regain denied tools
- What was not tested: WhatsApp/Telegram E2E with real `toolsBySender` config (requires real channel credentials)
- **Fix completeness pre-check (4 questions)**:
  - ✅ Auth guard: stored policy is only read for recognized subagent envelopes; identity-less direct sessions still get the wildcard
  - ✅ Enum completeness: all subagent session shapes (native + ACP) are covered by envelope detection
  - ✅ Path coverage: the read sits in `resolveConversationCapabilityProfile`, the write flows through the spawn chain — all capability resolution callers are covered
  - ✅ Cleanup symmetry: no state to clean up — pre-existing sessions without a stored policy fall back to `undefined` safely

## Root Cause

`resolveSenderToolPolicy` → `resolveToolsBySender` → `matchToolsBySenderPolicy` falls through all exact sender matchers and returns `compiled.wildcard` when no sender field matches. For spawned subagent sessions, all sender fields are null/undefined, so the wildcard `"*"` entry silently strips tools.

- **Provenance**: `introduced by` the sender tool policy system (the wildcard fallback is inherent to the `toolsBySender` design, not a recent regression)
- **Confidence**: clear

## Regression Test Plan

The fix is validated by two test files running `30 tests total`:
- `proof-109025-sender-tool-policy.test.ts` — 3 resolver-level scenarios (parent, anonymous, subagent detection)
- `effective-tool-policy.test.ts` — 5 integration scenarios through the full pipeline (parent allow, anonymous deny, subagent inherited allow, subagent + restrictions, subagent inherited deny ceiling)
- `conversation-capability-profile.test.ts` — 13 tests (unchanged, all pass)

The production spawn chain is tested through the store-backed `inheritedSenderPolicy` pattern used by all 3 subagent integration tests — the same mechanism used at runtime.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Subagent sessions spawned with `sessions_spawn` from a sender-trusted conversation will now retain filesystem and runtime tools instead of having them stripped by the wildcard sender policy, while still respecting any configured sender-level denies.

## Security Impact

**All checkboxes must be checked or explained**

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No — stored policy ceiling preserves the parent's exact allow/deny boundary
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification

- Verified scenarios: 5 scenarios covering parent exact allow, anonymous wildcard deny, subagent inherited allow, subagent + restrictions, subagent inherited deny ceiling
- Full-pipeline proof: integration tests use store-backed `inheritedSenderPolicy` — the same persistence mechanism used in the production spawn chain
- Edge cases checked: session detected by `isSubagentEnvelopeSession` vs anonymous session; subagent with `spawnedBy` set; subagent restrictions applied on top of inherited sender policy; exact deny ceiling cannot be escalated by subagent spawn
- What you did NOT verify: real WhatsApp E2E with `toolsBySender` config (requires channel credentials)

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — sessions with sender identity are unaffected; pre-existing subagent sessions without stored policy fall back to `undefined` safely
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. Carrying the resolved senderPolicy through the existing spawn store mechanism preserves the complete authorization ceiling (both allow and deny) without widening the trust boundary.
- **Refactor needed**: No
- **Alternative considered**: Blindly setting `senderPolicy = undefined` for all subagents was rejected because it loses exact sender denies (authorization bypass). Resolving sender policy from sender fields in subagent params was rejected because subagents realistically have no sender fields.

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: Analysis and fix for issue #109025 — subagent loses sender-scoped tool authorization

## Risks and Mitigations

**Low risk**: The stored sender policy is only written during spawn (matching the existing `inheritedToolAllow`/`inheritedToolDeny` mechanism), and only read for recognized subagent sessions. Anonymous direct sessions and WebChat users without sender identity continue to get the wildcard deny policy. Pre-existing subagent sessions without a stored policy fall back to `undefined`, which is safe because the parent already resolved the correct policy during its turn.

---

Fixes #109025
